analyst_observations.exit_144_cause_unknown: No Python traceback, no watchdog message, no crash output — just a clean cutoff mid-log. The task runner reports exit 144 = signal 16 = SIGURG on Darwin (unusual). Could be: (a) a hook script killed the process after a timeout, (b) an editor or IDE accidentally sent a signal to the subprocess, (c) the task runner's own supervisor terminated it. Not filing as a task because there's no reproducer and the cause isn't in the analyst's lane.
analyst_observations.ruler_was_23_pct_slower: Phase 3b took 291.9s vs R44/R47/R48 baseline of ~237s (+23%). Pre-run load was 1.75 (clean by any measure) but multi_key_niah@16K keys=5 alone was 2.4x slower (85s vs ~36s). This suggests some background process is competing for CPU during RULER's generation phases even without showing on load average. Something to watch on the next successful run.
